He played [[college basketball]] for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]], earning [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] honors in 2012. He was selected 40th overall in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and played for the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA G League]] before being traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2015, where he eventually became their franchise leader in three-pointers made. He has also played for the [[Washington Wizards]] and the [[Toronto Raptors]]. ==High school career== Barton, the No. 6-rated player in the nation in 2010, attended four schools in five years. He started his basketball career at [[Baltimore City College Basketball|Baltimore City College]], a public college preparatory high school, for two years before [[reclassification (education)|reclassifying]] and transferring to National Christian Academy in [[Fort Washington, Maryland]], to repeat his sophomore year. Barton then enrolled at Baltimore's [[Lake Clifton Eastern High School]] for his junior year. Then as a senior in 2009–10, he attended [[Brewster Academy]].[https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4925158 Barton ready for the Garden]{{cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2012/06/27/former-lake-clifton-star-will-barton-hoping-to-be-first-round-pick-in-nba-draft-2/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808052226/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2012-06-27/sports/bs-sp-will-barton-nba-draft-0628-20120626_1|url-status=live|archive-date=August 8, 2014|last=Letourneau|first=Connor|newspaper=The Baltimore Sun|title=Former Lake Clifton star Will Barton hoping to first-round pick in NBA draft|date=June 27, 2012|access-date=July 7, 2012}} Barton was rated the best shooting guard by [[Scout.com]] and [[ESPN.com]] in 2010.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=41&yr=2010 Scout.com College Basketball Team Recruiting over [[University of Arizona|Arizona]], [[University of Maryland, College Park|Maryland]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[Indiana University|Indiana]], and [[Villanova season, leading the Tigers in minutes per game at 30.6 and scoring with 12.3 points per game.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/235/year/2011/memphis-tigers Memphis Tigers Stats – 2010–11] Barton had a breakout sophomore season, leading the Tigers in points per game (18.0) and rebounds per game (8.0) en route to winning C-USA Player of the Year.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/235/year/2012/memphis-tigers Memphis Tigers Stats – 2011–12] For his career, he averaged 15.2 points, 6.5 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 32.9 minutes per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bartowi01.html#all_all_college_stats|title=Will Barton Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=December 2, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2012–2015)=== In March 2012, Barton decided to forgo his final two years of eligibility and declare for the [[2012 NBA draft]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7723474/memphis-tigers-guard-barton-declare-draft-source-says Will Barton to declare for draft] He was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 40th overall pick.[http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2012/06/nba_draft_blazers_take_memphis_will_barton_with_no.html NBA draft: Blazers take Memphis' Will Barton with No. 40 pick, trade 41st selection to Brooklyn] On December 7, 2012, he was assigned to the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. He was recalled on December 9, reassigned on January 6,{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20131029193513/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/3609/Default.aspx Nolan Smith, Will Barton Assigned to Idaho Stampede]}} and recalled again on January 9.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=12024 Trail Blazers recall Nolan Smith and Will Barton from D-League] He made his first NBA start on April 10, 2013, against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. On February 26, 2014, Barton recorded a season-high 20 points and a career-high 11 rebounds in 124–80 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20140226/BKNPOR/gameinfo.html Notebook: Trail Blazers 124, Nets 80] In a televised interview following the game, when asked by a reporter about a spontaneous "Will Barton" chant that had broken out late in the contest, the guard replied, "I like to think I'm the people's champ," thereby instantly giving birth to a new nickname and a Trail Blazers [[meme]].{{cite web | last=Meagher | first=Sean | url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2014/02/will_barton_the_peoples_champ_help_lead_trail_blaz.html | title=Will Barton, the people's champ, helps lead Trail Blazers to 124-80 win over Nets (postgame video) | work=OregonLive.com | date=February 26, 2014 | access-date=December 29, 2014}} He went on to record 17 points and six rebounds on May 12 to help Portland win Game 4 of their semi-final match-up against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. ===Denver Nuggets (2015–2022)=== [[File:Will Barton (cropped).jpg|thumb|Barton with the Denver Nuggets in 2020]] On February 19, 2015, Barton was traded, along with [[Víctor Claver]], [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]] and a lottery-protected 2016 first-round pick, to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Arron Afflalo]] and [[Alonzo Gee]].[http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-barton-claver-robinson-and-protected-first-round-pick-portland Nuggets Acquire Barton, Claver, Robinson and Protected First Round Pick From Portland] On August 7, 2015, Barton re-signed with the Nuggets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-darrell-arthur-will-barton-and-jameer-nelson|title=Nuggets Re-Sign Darrell Arthur, Will Barton and Jameer Nelson|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2015|access-date=August 7, 2015}} On November 13, 2015, he scored a career-high 26 points in a 107–98 win over the Houston Rockets.[http://www.nba.com/games/20151113/HOUDEN/gameinfo.html Gallinari's scores 27 points, Nuggets top Rockets 107-98] He topped that mark on December 20 with 32 points against the New Orleans Pelicans.[http://www.nba.com/games/20151220/NOPDEN/gameinfo.html Davis leads Pelicans to 130-125 win over Nuggets] Barton's strong pre-Christmas play earned him recognition as a possible contender for the 2015–16 Sixth Man of the Year award.[http://www.basketballinsiders.com/nba-am-barton-making-case-for-sixth-man-honors/ NBA AM: Barton Making Case For Sixth Man Honors] Over the Nuggets' first 29 games of the season, Barton averaged 15.7 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.1 steals in 29.0 minutes per game off the bench.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bartowi01/gamelog/2016/ Will Barton 2015-16 Game Log] Barton appeared in just six of the Nuggets' first 18 games of the 2016–17 season. He played in the first three games before missing the next nine after spraining his left ankle. He then returned for three before missing another for personal reasons, and then a further two with another left ankle complaint.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899723|title=Whiteside's double-double lifts Heat over Nuggets 106-98|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=December 1, 2016}} On January 17, 2017, he had season highs of 26 points and eight assists in a 127–121 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900047|title=Jokic scores 29, Nuggets hold off struggling Lakers 127-121|work=ESPN.com|date=January 17, 2017|access-date=January 18, 2017}} On February 6, 2017, he scored a then season-high 31 points and hit five three-pointers in a 110–87 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900181|title=Barton scores 31 in Nuggets' 110-87 win over Mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=February 6, 2017|access-date=February 7, 2017}} On March 13, 2017, in a 129–101 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], Barton scored 22 points and went 3 of 4 behind the arc and 6 of 9 overall in his most productive outing since the All-Star break. Prior to the game against the Lakers, Barton had made just five of his previous 21 three-point tries.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900393|title=Barton, Murray each score 22, Nuggets beat Lakers 129-101|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 14, 2017}} On March 16, 2017, he scored a career-high 35 points in a 129–114 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900413|title=Barton scores 35 points, lead Nuggets over Clippers 129-114|work=ESPN.com|date=March 16, 2017|access-date=March 17, 2017}} On November 11, 2017, Barton had season highs with 26 points and nine rebounds in a 125–107 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974936|title=Murray scores career-high 32 as Nuggets beat Magic, 125-107|work=ESPN.com|date=November 11, 2017|access-date=November 11, 2017}} On November 30, 2017, Barton capped a career-high 37 points with a driving layup with 3.2 seconds left to lift the Nuggets to a 111–110 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975066|title=Barton scores 37 points, Nuggets rally to beat Bulls 111-110|work=ESPN.com|date=November 30, 2017|access-date=December 1, 2017}} On February 3, 2018, he scored a team-high 25 points in a 115–108 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975528|title=Jokic makes go-ahead 3-pointer, Nuggets top Warriors 115-108|work=ESPN.com|date=February 3, 2018|access-date=February 4, 2018}} On July 9, 2018, Barton re-signed with the Nuggets.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/barton-re-sign-contract-070918|title=Nuggets Re-Sign Free Agent Will Barton|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2018|access-date=July 9, 2018}} On October 20, 2018, in just the second game of the season, Barton injured his right hip on a reverse layup in the third quarter of Denver's 119–91 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070716|title=Jokic's triple-double leads Nuggets past Suns 119-91|work=ESPN.com|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2018}} He was subsequently ruled out for five to six weeks after undergoing surgery on October 23.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25055157/will-barton-denver-nuggets-needs-hip-surgery-5-6-weeks|title=Nuggets' Will Barton to undergo surgery to repair adductor muscle injury|work=ESPN.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=October 22, 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/barton-surgery-102418-2|title=Will Barton Undergoes Successful web|last=Dempsey|first=Christopher|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/barton-is-back-011219|title=Barton's Back: The Nuggets Starter Makes Long-Awaited Return from Injury|work=NBA.com|date=January
